name: infra_pyspark_mllib
title: Spark MLlib: same method names as sklearn, a different library, and a real leak MLView must not guess at
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-infra: the unsupported-framework precision trap with maximum name collision
note: Every forbidden row below is a name collision with scikit-learn: StandardScaler.fit, Pipeline.fit, CrossValidator.fit, RandomForestClassifier.fit, randomSplit. MLView resolves none of them, reports nothing, and declares an `unresolved_callee` gap naming pyspark plus two `untagged_dataflow` gaps - which is the right answer and the claim this program guards. There IS a real leak here (scaler.fit(frame) at line 63 on the whole DataFrame, randomSplit at line 68), and MLView not finding it is a known blindness, not a defect: a Spark StandardScaler is not an sklearn.preprocessing row and iron law 1 forbids matching on the bare attribute name. One reporting defect is visible: the dataEntry answer says `No data entry was detected: nothing in this workspace builds a dataset or a loader` with no qualifier, while the objective and evaluation answers on the same document both carry `and 13 call(s) could not be read`. See the domain-infra round-2 report, finding INFRA-R2-12.
stagesObserved: config, preprocess and train present (three function nodes and the argparse config); data, model, objective, eval and deliver reported absent, with the 13 unreadable pyspark calls named in the diagnostics. `workspace.frameworks` is empty, which is honest.

forbidden.why: the fit at line 63 is pyspark.ml.feature.StandardScaler.fit, not sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler.fit; it resolves to nothing and iron law 1 forbids matching the bare name. The leak is real and the honest answer is the pyspark coverage gap, not a finding
same reason: every .fit() in this file belongs to pyspark.ml
CrossValidator at line 79 is pyspark.ml.tuning.CrossValidator and its estimator IS a pyspark.ml.Pipeline; neither resolves, and both are correct usage in any case
randomSplit is a Spark DataFrame method, there is no temporal column in this job, and no sklearn splitter is called
there is no torch DataLoader in this workspace
there is no torch DataLoader in this workspace
BinaryClassificationEvaluator.evaluate at line 85 is a Spark evaluator; it takes a predictions DataFrame, not a (y_true, y_pred) pair
areaUnderROC here is computed by Spark from the rawPrediction column, which is a score column by construction
SEED = 31 is passed to randomSplit (line 68), to RandomForestClassifier (line 70) and to CrossValidator (line 79); those are the only random sources in a Spark job
randomSplit passes seed=SEED at line 68, and it is not an sklearn splitter in any case
the save at line 104 is Spark's MLWriter, not torch.save, and nothing in this file calls torch.load

unsupported.why: LABEL CORRECTED in hardening round 2: MLV117 is not a built rule - it carries the status **later** in docs/ISSUE_RULES.md section 1 - so a label for it can never be satisfied and can never be violated. `analyzer/tests/accuracy/test_accuracy.py::test_every_labelled_code_is_a_real_rule` rejects one, and this row turned that shipped test red. The observation is kept verbatim here so the row can be restored the day the rule ships. Original verdict `forbidden`, original note: randomSplit has no stratify= parameter to be missing; this is not sklearn
